Published paper and verification package: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23430475 (https://zenodo.org/records/23430475).

An explicitly expository original-ball path corollary of Lenzhen–Rafi’s established uniform quasiconvexity theorem. For each fixed closed oriented surface of genus at least two, every pair of points in any original closed half-log Teichmüller ball has a continuous rectifiable path inside that same ball with length at most its ambient distance plus 4c_g. One finite topology-dependent c_g works for all centers, radii and pairs. Radial endpoint retreat followed by a minimizing segment gives the deduction and an affirmative derivation of Farb’s Question 3.5 from prior geometry.

All substantive Teichmüller estimates are credited to Lenzhen–Rafi. Historical priority for the elementary lemma and exact corollary is unestablished; no new substantive theorem, worldwide firstness, current openness, numerical or genus-uniform constant, or optimal Teichmüller bound is claimed. Kerckhoff’s formula and Fortier Bourque–Rafi’s metric and nonconvexity interfaces are credited. Petyt–Zalloum’s 2024/2026 dual wall-space almost convexity uses a different metric, with no comparison of numerical constants. A bounded priority audit does not certify absence of prior work.

The deposit includes the full proof, TeX source, scope supplement, byte-preserved theoretical original and authored independent adversarial mathematical and source audits. No original executable was submitted; these are written verification materials, not a computational or proof-assistant certificate. Third-party paper bodies are omitted. AI tools were used extensively in deriving, verifying, adversarial review, source auditing and preparation. This is an unrefereed expository preprint; conventional human peer review and journal acceptance are not claimed.

## Accepted scope and review Each fixed closed genus g>=2 has c_g so every pair in any original closed Teichmuller ball admits an in-ball path of length <= ambient distance+4c_g, giving every fixed k detour bound. No gap asserted for fixed closed genus; numerical c_g, uniform-in-genus and punctured variants not claimed. The result is accepted at the exact audited head `6322305d37b8131f034a1b4c3c5e861e4b04844f`. 2 fresh independent complete AI whole-package reviews were completed, with the final review finding zero actionable issues. Subsequent bounded administrative adoption is recorded in the current external ROOT final seal; earlier status/counter/hold fields remain dated history. Prior mathematical results and proof dependencies are credited. Historical novelty and worldwide current openness are unestablished. AI tools were used extensively; this is an unrefereed preprint, without conventional human peer review or formal proof certification. The repository Zenodo uploader verified the exact reviewed metadata and PDF/support bytes. The Google Workspace CLI recorded the DOI/details in the requested tracker with exact read-back. No GitHub release is created. Current audit and publication receipts: `audits/pr1033_11000026`.
Preserved original PR description: dated submission history ## Result For each fixed closed oriented genus g ≥ 2, every pair of points in every original closed Teichmüller ball admits a continuous rectifiable path inside that same ball of length at most its ambient distance plus 4c_g. Consequently N_g(k) = k + 4c_g for every fixed k > 0, including the distance-two bound 2 + 4c_g. The metric is the actual half-log-dilatation Teichmüller metric. The constant depends only on genus; no numerical or uniform-in-genus value is claimed. ## Mathematical evidence and attribution This draft contains the full authored proof, its byte-identical audited version, and the full byte-identical independent AI mathematical audit. The audit reports PASS with no blocking mathematical finding. The public proof applies exactly its two optional editorial suggestions, documented in the README: identify Theorem 15 as the extremal-length part of Theorem A, and use “Consequently” before the intrinsic-distance bound. The substantive Teichmüller input is Anna Lenzhen and Kasra Rafi, [*Length of a curve is quasi-convex along a Teichmüller geodesic*, JDG 88 (2011), 267–295](https://www.math.toronto.edu/rafi/Papers/Convexity.pdf), Theorems C and 17. The added general metric argument retreats endpoints before invoking the uniform additive quasiconvexity theorem and then concatenates three geodesic pieces. Published geodesic existence is also used. This is an AI mathematical audit, not human peer review or formal proof-assistant verification. No historical novelty or priority is claimed. One substantive approach was used out of a limit of five. The theorem is a theoretical deduction; no substantive computational experiment was required or used as mathematical evidence. Hashes, sizes, file comparisons, and patch replay are publication-integrity checks only. ## Exact scope Add only the eight files listed below under `unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/11000026/`. The package contains proof, audit, acceptance/status, public source metadata, and an exact file manifest. It contains no executable scripts, test fixtures, copied third-party source documents, dataset contents, private sources, or private coordination material.
